args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy on v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate had also been unhealthy in staging before it went to production.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. It's now running in all three regions, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Rolling back to a release that was already healthy didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure should be found before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
